comparison: Perfect agreement on puncta formation (C1, C10-C14). Both evaluations find strong support for Met4 and Met32 forming co-localized puncta structures under inducing conditions, with reviewers explicitly affirming this finding as a key strength.

Perfect agreement on in vitro LLPS evidence (C2, C15-C23). Both evaluations support the formation of Met32-driven condensates with Met4 colocalization. OpenEval notes Met4 alone remains diffusive, while peer reviewers identify Met32 as the driver without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on puncta-gene colocalization (C3, C24-C29). Both evaluations affirm the ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and imaging evidence showing Met4 puncta colocalize with target genes like MET6 and MET13, with no concerns raised about the data quality.

Strong disagreement on 3D gene clustering mechanism (C4, C30-C34). OpenEval finds the MTAC data and Met4 degradation experiments provide strong support, while peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, noting the evidence is correlative and fails to show condensates per se drive clustering.

Agreement on enhanced transcription at hotspots (C5, C35-C37, C40-C45), though peer review includes C38-C39 and C73 while OpenEval addresses these separately. Both strongly support the pathway-specific transcriptional enhancement with distance-dependent effects, with peer reviewers particularly praising the control experiments.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretation of IDR truncation (C6-C7, C46-C53, C75). OpenEval finds strong functional evidence linking condensation to gene regulation, while peer reviewers rate this as UNCERTAIN, noting the genetic approach yields ambiguous results and correlation rather than causation, with IDR deletion potentially affecting other molecular interactions.

Disagreement on integrative model (C8-C9, C76-C77, C87). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by totality of evidence despite acknowledging speculation, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the lack of mechanistic proof that condensates per se drive gene clustering and the correlative nature of the evidence.

OpenEval addresses negative result on Met4 intensity upon reporter insertion (C38-C39) as a separate finding, while peer review includes these claims within the broader transcriptional enhancement evaluation (R5). Both accept the imaging data showing no local Met4 increase.

Agreement on background and contextual claims (C54-C85 with high overlap). Both evaluations support these literature citations and established biological knowledge as appropriate context. OpenEval includes C73 separately while peer review includes C86; neither questions the cited work.

OpenEval separately evaluates control data at basal loci (C75) as supported evidence for selective condensate effects, while peer review includes C75 within the broader IDR truncation evaluation (R6) but rates the mechanistic interpretation as uncertain.
